D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official hosted tool reference documents reads and watchlist writes/deletes; it does not publish hosted tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint). The old local example annotates ChatCBI readOnlyHint=true and openWorldHint=true, but it is a different server. 2. No server-enforced confirmation flow is documented. Tool descriptions recommend or explain behavior; write operations are exposed directly. 3. OAuth scopes are exactly openid, email, profile; no data-specific scopes are advertised. Subscription and user sign-in are required; client connection may require admin approval. Role inheritance is reflected in watchlist permissions; docs distinguish owner/read_write/read. Token lifetime/revocation not found. 4. No read-only endpoint, toolset filter, query-free mode, or sandbox/production split found. 5. Tool guidance limits query_context to relevant entity disambiguation and says not to pass the user's message or unrelated details. No general PII masking or field-scope rule found. 6. Tool-level bounds include defaults and caps: search results, per-company lists, selector fan-out, watchlist edits (up to 200 orgs/1000 values), and some result-cell truncation. search_companies extended_thinking allows up to two minutes. Pricing is consumption-based, but call costs/quotas not published. 7. Docs describe invalid/unresolved inputs, type mismatch handling, limits, and alias/deprecation guidance; no general unknown-argument policy or operator override is documented. 8. log_app_event records UI telemetry attributed to the current user/team; general audit logs, retention, opt-out, and telemetry defaults are not documented. 9. No feedback/rating/survey tools found in the full official list. log_app_event is telemetry, not feedback. No documented upsell response. 10. Tool descriptions contain behavioral directions and citation guidance; no hosted skill-loading tool documented. The deprecated local example has a server instruction, not evidence for the hosted endpoint. 11. Some tools act on the current user's watchlists, and a search ID supports later pagination; durable agent-specific memory is not documented. 12. One hosted endpoint is documented; strategy map has a companion MCP App. No proxy hierarchy or sub-server routing is documented. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or equivalent escape hatch appears in the official action list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: “Do NOT use it to look up or verify one specific named company, or to check attributes of a list of named companies” — search_companies.
“Always show the citation source URL in your answer - the results must be cited.” — search_companies.
“Prefer several narrow searches over one sprawling multi-sector search.” — search_companies.
“Do not pass the user's message or any unrelated details.” — query_context parameter guidance.
“Never delete and recreate a column to change its options or format — that wipes every value in it.” — add_watchlist_column.
“Pass a label back to set_watchlist_cell_values, never an id.” — add_watchlist_column.
“To compare multiple earnings periods, call this tool in parallel once per period.” — get_earnings_call_transcript.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: One hosted endpoint with a documented flat set of 45 tools. The strategy-map tool has a companion MCP App, but no hierarchy or dynamically selected sub-server toolsets are described.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool reference at https://mcp.cbinsights.com/docs-portal.md names 45 tools and states a total of 45 (23 Entity Data, 6 Search, 16 Other). Three additional names absent from that reference are appended from the Claude connector directory: api_chatcbi, api_rag, company_advanced_search. Catalogue counts differ: Claude directory lists 15; Agentman reports 40; mcp.so reports 40; Agent Discoverability lists 38; Manufact describes 15; MarTechDB reports one documented tool, ChatCBI, consistent with the deprecated local example rather than the hosted reference. Counts may reflect different snapshots or surfaces; see contradictions.

E_aggregated.token_method: Hosted initialize instructions and verbatim tool definitions with annotations are not available as a complete serialized MCP context. Public code belongs to a separate deprecated self-hosted server, so its token count is not used for this endpoint.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The vendor presents the Strategy Terminal, standalone Team of Agents, mobile app, and browser extension as separate products; these are not exposed as actions in the hosted MCP reference. The reference documents no general REST passthrough, API-key creation, subscription purchase, or arbitrary data export beyond its named tools. This describes documented MCP coverage, not the full product/API feature set.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Tool descriptions provide query and selection guidance, including “Always show the citation source URL in your answer - the results must be cited.” and warnings to review potentially off-target search results. These are client/agent instructions; hosted enforcement is not established by the docs.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Pricing page states “No training on your data.” Additional Terms say customers remain responsible for downstream storage and use after Licensed Materials are transmitted to their systems or AI tools, and require attribution to CB Insights in specified contexts. The relevant terms also restrict use of Licensed Materials to defined permitted purposes.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor describes the hosted MCP server as a way to securely access CB Insights data and capabilities, and the pricing page offers direct access to CB Insights intelligence through MCP.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth gates endpoint access and watchlist tools describe permission checks, but public implementation for the hosted service was not available. No server-side evidence was found for the no-training claim, downstream retention controls, or attribution enforcement; those remain documentation/contract statements in the reviewed sources.

contradictions: The hosted official tool reference states 45 tools. Catalogue snapshots report 40 (Agentman, mcp.so), 38 (Agent Discoverability), or 15 (Claude directory and Manufact); those catalogues omit official tools or reflect different snapshots.

Claude directory lists api_chatcbi, api_rag, and company_advanced_search, which are absent from the current official hosted list; they are retained as third-party-only entries with unknown default availability. The official repository's ChatCBI tool belongs to the separately identified deprecated self-hosted variant and is not added to actions.json.
MarTechDB reports a single documented ChatCBI tool, which matches the deprecated public self-hosted example, while the current hosted reference lists 45 differently named tools.
observations_for_research: The hosted reference carries extensive agent-facing workflow guidance in tool descriptions, including search selection, citation, result review, and watchlist edit warnings.

The OAuth scope list is identity-oriented (openid, email, profile), while the hosted tools expose CB Insights data and user-specific watchlist operations; the metadata does not enumerate separate data permissions.
A dedicated log_app_event tool permits MCP Apps to submit interaction telemetry attributed to a user/team.
Documentation distinguishes default concise/full presets and provides per-tool bounds, selectors, and permission-aware behavior.
notes: Inspected prepared links.json, links_check.txt, all 60 page files including scripts, and the local official repository. The official hosted reference is a complete 45-tool list. The endpoint root returned HTTP 405 for page retrieval; supplied OAuth metadata was used as given. The local repository is explicitly deprecated and distinct from the hosted service. Catalogue warnings and count differences are treated as catalogue claims, not as hosted implementation evidence. Pricing amounts, hosted protocol version, tool annotations, token lifetime/revocation, initialize instructions, and a hosted source-code implementation were not found.
